title: AugServe: Adaptive Request Scheduling for Augmented Large Language Model Inference Serving
technique: state-aware request scheduling (value density with waiting-time term, two-stage) + dynamic batch-level token budget from free and reclaimable GPU memory

optimized_metrics.evidence: Our goal is to maximize goodput in augmented LLM inference, accounting for both request service rates and queuing delays.
AugServe, an efficient augmented LLM inference serving framework that mitigates request queuing latency and improves effective throughput
SLOs are set as TTFT<1s and normalized latency<10x single-iteration time
SLOs are set as TTFT<1s and normalized latency<10x single-iteration time

headline_claim.text: AugServe achieves 6.5x and 4.7x higher effective throughput than vLLM and INFERCEPT, respectively.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: effective throughput (or goodput), defined as the volume of requests processed per unit time that successfully satisfy these SLO requirements
goodput (number of SLO-satisfying requests per unit time)
metric_definitions.notes: SLO is joint TTFT and normalized latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: normalized latency (end-to-end latency divided by output length)
SLO attainment (i.e., the fraction of requests meeting SLOs, Appendix D.8)

slo_spec: TTFT < 1 s and normalized latency < 10x single-iteration time (following prior work); goodput counts requests meeting both
load_regime: request-rate sweep; W1 Poisson over 30 min, W2 Gamma arrivals with varying CV
tradeoff_acknowledged: SJF-style throughput priority vs fairness/starvation traded via beta weight on waiting time
extractor_notes: Goodput is clearly the objective; queueing delay is the mechanism. Headline is 'effective throughput' = goodput.
